name: Neon Eclipse: Dominium
detailed_description:
Summary
Neon Eclipse: Dominium is a 2D cyberpunk metroidvania where you become a shadow warrior fighting to dismantle a dystopian empire ruled by the Iron Dominion, a mega-corporation that controls humanity through technology and terror. Choose between three unique ninjas—each with distinct abilities (genetic enhancements, cybernetic weaponry, or pure martial mastery)—to infiltrate interconnected dystopian cities, sabotage high-tech facilities, and overthrow biomechanical tyrants. Blend stealth, combat, and moral choices to carve your path in a world where every decision shapes the future.

Key Features

  • 3 Unique Ninjas: Master Motoichi’s genetic agility, Aiko’s lethal cyber-implants, or Marcos’s traditional techniques—each with their own playstyle and upgrades.

  • Cyberpunk Metroidvania: Explore sprawling, interconnected environments—from neon-lit slums to AI-controlled fortresses—unlocking abilities to access hidden zones and secrets.

  • Stealth & Combat: Sabotage enemies silently or unleash chaos with dynamic combat. Outsmart biomechanical bosses with strategy and skill.

  • Moral Choices: Ally with rebels, betray factions, or walk a solitary path. Your decisions alter alliances, missions, and the game’s ending.

  • Upgrade System: Customize your ninja with cyberware, genetic boosts, or ancient relics to match your tactics.

The World of 22XX
In a future where corporations rule with iron fists, the Iron Dominion has enslaved humanity through surveillance, propaganda, and biomechanical armies. As part of the Eclipse Corps—a rogue ninja alliance—you’ll infiltrate their strongholds, expose their plans for global domination, and rally resistance fighters. But trust is scarce: allies may betray you, and even your upgrades come with a price.

Face the Dominion
From hacking security grids to dueling cyborg warlords, every mission demands adaptability. Will you exploit the Dominion’s technology against them, or reject it to hone your primal skills? The choice is yours—but the cost of failure is extinction.
